thread.title: The easy money has already been made in this market, says Howard Marks

author: morningstar.com
title: The easy money has already been made in this market, says Howard Marks
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
As everyone keeps wondering what might finally rock this unflappable market, it's not a bad time to score a view from the mountaintop.
So, you CEOs and other bigwigs braving snowy Davos this week -- even ditching limos for trains in some hard-luck cases (https://www.theguardian.com/business/2018/jan/23/snow-falling-on-leaders-exceptional-winter-weather-delays-vip-arrivals-to-davos) -- we welcome your thoughts, especially if you've spotted a sell signal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pay-close-attention-to-the-message-out-of-davos-then-unload-your-stocks-2018-01-23).
Bridgewater's Ray Dalio said in Switzerland that investors are fools to stay in cash (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/head-of-worlds-largest-hedge-fund-says-if-youre-holding-cash-youre-going-to-feel-pretty-stupid-2018-01-23), and UBS exec Axel Weber sounds worried about complacency (https://www.wsj.com/articles/as-markets-and-growth-steam-ahead-signs-of-caution-emerge-1516740176). J.P. Morgan's Jacob Frenkel's (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/01/24/davos-rapid-rise-in-global-debt-is-a-major-concern-jp-morgan-international-chair-says.html) concern is that "problems arise, always, when you are overly optimistic." There will be plenty more spouting off in the next couple of days, so stay alert.
It's back down to earth, so to speak, with our call of the day, from Oaktree Capital's Howard Marks. He says "the easy money has been made" in this market, so "considerable caution" is advised.
The S&P 500 has roughly quadrupled from its 2009 low, Marks notes.
"It was certainly easier for the P/E ratio to go from the low teens in 2011-12 to 25 today than it would be for it to double again from here," he writes in his latest memo. "Thus, the one thing we can say for sure is that the current prospects for making money in U.S. equities aren't what they were half a dozen years ago."
Now you might be rolling your eyes at the sight of what looks like another bear, but Marks says he doesn't mean get out, because the near-term economic outlook is positive, interest rates are low, and most investors need the return stocks can offer.
However, given high asset prices and fairly risky behavior, he warns that this is not the time to get aggressive. His memo is packed, and you can read it all here (https://www.oaktreecapital.com/docs/default-source/memos/latest-thinking.pdf).
Futures are pointing to another up day for stocks, while the dollar is getting absolutely kicked in the teeth thanks to another voice in the Davos wilderness this morning. Hang onto your hats today.
(https://twitter.com/StockCats/status/955948991136632833)
Key market gauges
Futures for the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 are higher. Asia (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-cool-off-following-recent-hot-streak-2018-01-23) and Europe have been mixed bags (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-waver-as-euro-rallies-suez-tanks-after-profit-warning-2018-01-24).
The dollar index sank to a fresh three-year low below 90 as Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin told reporters in Davos that a weaker greenback is good for trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-plunges-to-3-year-low-after-mnuchin-cheers-weaker-greenback-2018-01-24). Oil is steady ahead of U.S. supply data, while natural gas is soaring (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/natural-gas-soars-with-the-leap-setting-off-a-trading-halt-2018-01-24) -- with more on that in our chart of the day. On the crypto front, bitcoin is closing in on $11,000.
See the Market Snapshot (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-futures-rise-as-market-rally-shows-no-sign-of-abatement-2018-01-24) for the latest action.
The buzz
GE (GE) is jumping despite a surprise loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ges-stock-surges-despite-surprise-loss-and-revenue-miss-as-power-and-oil-gas-revenue-beats-2018-01-24). Also on the earnings docket before the open: Comcast (CMCSA) and United Tech (UTX)
Ford is due to report after the close, and analysts don't sound that hopeful (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ford-earnings-disappointing-outlook-stock-weakness-among-stumbling-blocks-2018-01-19).
Intel earnings preview:About those chip hacks.. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/intel-earnings-all-eyes-on-chip-hack-fixes-data-center-growth-2018-01-23).
Texas Instruments (TXN) is getting creamed after the chip maker delivered in-line results and a modest outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/texas-instruments-shares-fall-on-in-line-results-modest-outlook-2018-01-23).
Qualcomm (QCOM) has been slapped with a $1.23 billion fine by the EU over paying (AAPL) to exclusively use its chips (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/qualcomm-fined-123-billion-by-eu-for-payments-to-apple-for-chip-exclusivity-2018-01-24).
Moon travel ain't easy, and Google (GOOGL) (GOOGL)has called off its Lunar XPrize competition (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/google-lunar-xprize-ends-because-getting-to-the-moon-is-hard-2018-01-23). No one is getting the $30 million grand prize.
After the opening bell, Markit is due to offer readings on manufacturing and services, and report on existing home sales is slated to arrive as well.
In Davos, protesters who aren't fans of President Trump have caused a little trouble (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-davos-meeting-protests/swiss-marchers-protest-against-trump-break-through-davos-security-cordon-idUSKBN1FC2OI).
Also at the Swiss confab, Baidu's (BIDU) Ya-Qin Zhang hinted at "exciting deals" ahead for video content (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/01/24/baidu-hints-at-further-deals-to-bring-netflix-content-to-china.html). The "Google of China" already has a content agreement with Netflix (NFLX) .
The chart
Natural gas shot up yesterday and it's up big again today.
The credit for natty's leap is going to indications that freezing weather (like what was seen as 2018 kicked off) could be headed to a swath of the U.S. in early February. Expect to hear more talk about a so-called polar vortex in the next couple of sessions.
(https://twitter.com/BigJoeBastardi/status/955513110449836032)
The Quote:
"It is nothing but sobering to know that the person who sat across from you at the lunch table went home to squalor and filth, while you went home to a warm meal and a bedtime story." --Taha Muntajibuddin, a pediatrician who went to school with the oldest of the 13 siblings allegedly tortured by their parents.
In a Facebook post, he has recalled going to grade school with the now-29-year-old, including how she was teased (http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-turpin-oldest-child-school-20180123-story.html) for being smelly, skinny and wearing the same clothes.
Prosecutors are aiming to block those parents in California from contacting the kids (https://edition.cnn.com/2018/01/23/us/turpins-child-torture-allegations/index.html).
Random reads
Super Bowl ticket prices sure don't look like they are going up (https://www.zerohedge.com/news/2018-01-23/super-bowl-ticket-prices-are-falling).
MPR says Garrison Keillor wasn't fired for just one incident (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/garrison-keillors-firing-came-after-dozens-of-accusations-2018-01-23).
Widespread sexual harassment has been exposed at this dinner (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/widespread-sexual-harassment-exposed-at-charity-dinner-for-uks-business-elite-2018-01-24) for elites.
Emotional shoppers seem to like Tide Pods and Clorox (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-americans-emotionally-spend-they-buy-toilet-paper-and-bleach-2017-03-23).
Camels were kicked out of a beauty contest (http://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-5302989/Camels-disqualified-Saudi-beauty-contest-Botox.html) for using botox. Really.
Trump reportedly asked the acting FBI director who got his vote in 2016 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-asked-acting-fbi-director-who-he-voted-for-report-2018-01-23).
Meanwhile, Robert Mueller has got some questions (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mueller-seeks-to-question-trump-about-flynn-comey-reports-2018-01-23).
